### The Antibiotic Substance Entries Are Inconsistent {#sec-problem-details-30}

The surveillance end form records, for each systemic antibiotic substance the infant received, the substance and the number of days on which it was given, in up to nine substance entries.
An entry holds a substance together with its days.
A substance day is an antibiotic day and an antibiotic day is a patient day, so the days of one substance can exceed neither the total antibiotic days nor the patient days.
The protocol counts a substance's days cumulatively: one entry holds the days of all the treatment courses in which the infant received the substance.

Four messages report a violation of these rules: a substance recorded without its days or days recorded without a substance; a substance whose days exceed the total antibiotic days or the patient days, which includes a substance recorded on a form whose total antibiotic days are zero; the same substance recorded in two entries; and a substance whose entries together record more days than the total antibiotic days.
The form shows the first entry once antibiotic days are entered and each further entry once the previous one holds a substance.
It asks for the substance of the first entry and for the days of every entry whose substance is chosen, and it insists on what it asks for only when the form is completed.
It does not ask for the substance of entries 2 to 9 when their days are entered, so days without a substance can be recorded on any form, and a substance without its days on a form that is not completed yet or that was written by a tool that does not apply these checks.
The other three shapes are not checked when the data is entered.

A substance recorded in two entries is most often one entry for each treatment course.
The analyses add up a substance's entries, so such entries do not distort the results, and the message is a warning, although the protocol asks for one entry.
If the same course was entered twice, however, its days are counted twice.
The message therefore says what the entries' days suggest: entries with different days are most likely one for each course, and entries with the same days may be one course entered twice.
Entries that together record more days than the total antibiotic days cannot all be separate courses, so their message is no warning: a course was entered twice, an entry records too many days, or the total antibiotic days are too few.

Please open the surveillance end form (see @sec-solution-15), reopen it for editing if it is completed (see @sec-solution-9) and complete, correct or clear the entries concerned.
When a substance appears in two entries for separate courses, enter the days of all its courses in the entry with the lower number and remove the other entry.
When the same course was entered twice, remove the entry with the higher number.
When the total antibiotic days are too few, correct them.

Remove an entry with care.
The form hides an entry while the entry before it holds no substance, and Tracker Capture blanks out the values of an entry it hides.
It says so for each of the entry's two fields in a message, in English whatever the language of the interface, which names the field and says it was blanked out and hidden by your last action.
Clearing an entry that other entries follow therefore blanks out the entry after it, and with a later change the one after that.
To remove an entry that other entries follow, choose in it the substance of the last entry that holds one, without clearing it first, and enter that entry's days; then clear the substance and the days of that last entry.
To remove the last entry that holds a substance, clear its substance and its days.
